title: Evaluating Instrument-Centered AI Agents for Table-Top Science Experiments
summary: In a virtual condensed-matter laboratory benchmark, agents performed better on measurement than scientific analysis, and an analysis-only reference-data ablation closed about two-thirds of that gap. Results are limited to virtual instruments and the tested tasks.
ai_technology: commercial coding agents operate QCoDeS virtual instruments through instrMCP; an ablation supplies clean reference data without a measurement session
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: In a virtual condensed-matter laboratory benchmark, agents performed better on measurement than scientific analysis, and an analysis-only reference-data ablation closed about two-thirds of that gap. Results are limited to virtual instruments and the tested tasks. Evaluation: 37 reconstructed tasks; 10 agent configurations, five runs per task/configuration (1,850 runs); rubric grading with second-judge audit
evidence.unknown: The evaluation is limited to the virtual instruments and benchmark tasks; physical laboratory performance is not established.
evidence.ai_role: commercial coding agents operate QCoDeS virtual instruments through instrMCP; an ablation supplies clean reference data without a measurement session.
